metadata.title: Finite generation conjectures for cohomology over finite fields

extraction_notes.note: Lead-in sentences 'Since ... we have' and 'As in Proposition 2.4, we obtain' run straight into the result environment without punctuation; taken as prose proof nodes ending at the environment.
Pirutka's construction is stated twice with different hypotheses (surface in the introduction, dimension-5 variety in 3.1), so kept as two external theorems rather than one repeated node.
The first case of the proof of Theorem 2.13 reads 'If $n=0$' though the theorem already assumes n=0; it is evidently the prime-to-p case.

Motivational sentences (e.g. Kato homology generalization, 'Considering finite coefficients allows...', Tate's original conjecture remark) and the sentence on the degree shift of gamma were left in no node.

nodes.name: Bass' conjecture
nodes.statement: Bass conjectured that for a regular scheme $X$ of finite type over the integers, the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated \cite{bassln342}.
assumptions: $X$ of finite type over the integers
conclusions: the higher algebraic $K$-groups are finitely generated
nodes.statement_short: Higher algebraic K-groups of regular schemes of finite type over Z are finitely generated.

nodes.name: Weil-etale cohomology
nodes.statement: Still for $X$ of finite type over a finite field, LIchtenbaum's Weil-etale cohomology $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_GR\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, where $G$ is the Weil-group of the finite field.
nodes.statement_short: Weil-etale cohomology is the cohomology of the Weil-group derived functor applied to etale cohomology over the algebraic closure.

nodes.name: Finite generation of Weil-etale cohomology is equivalent to Tate and Beilinson
nodes.statement: Using ideas of Kahn, we showed in \cite{ichweilI} that the finite generation of $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ for smooth and proper $X$ is equivalent to the strong form of Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture.
conclusions: the finite generation of $H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ for smooth and proper $X$ is equivalent to the strong form of Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture
equivalent_conditions: the strong form of Tate's and Beilinson's conjecture

nodes.name: Frobenius cohomology
nodes.statement: The purpose of this article is to relate the two finite generaton conjectures with the help of an intermediate cohomology theory $H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, which we call Frobenius cohomology. It is defined as the cohomology of $R\Gamma_G{{\mathbb Z}}(n)(\bar X)$, where ${{\mathbb Z}}(n)$ is Bloch's cycle complex shifted appropriately.
nodes.statement_short: Frobenius cohomology is the cohomology of the Weil-group derived functor applied to Bloch's cycle complex over the algebraic closure.

nodes.name: Kato cohomology
nodes.statement: In fact they lie in a diagram \begin{equation}\begin{CD} @>>>H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\alpha >>H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\beta>> H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))@>>> \end{CD}\end{equation} with groups $H^i_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))=H^i({{\mathbb Z}}(n)(\bar X)_G)$ called Kato cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: Motivic, Frobenius and Kato cohomology fit in a long exact row mapping to etale and Weil-etale cohomology; Kato cohomology is the coinvariant cycle complex cohomology.

nodes.statement: \begin{CD} @>>>H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\alpha >>H^i_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\beta>> H^{i-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>\gamma>>\\ @EEE @Vf VV @Vg VV @VhVV \\ @>>> H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) @>>> H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))@>>> \end{CD}

nodes.name: Geometric Frobenius and Weil group
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi$ be the geometric Frobenius, and $G=\langle \varphi\rangle$ be the Weil group of ${{\mathbb F}}_q$.

nodes.name: Bloch's cycle complex shifted by 2n
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)$ be the cycle complex defined by Bloch shifted by $2n$, so that $$H_i({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)) = CH_n(X,i-2n).$$

nodes.statement: This agrees with motivic cohomology $H^{2d-i}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(d-n))$ for smooth $X$ of pure dimension $d$ by \cite{voevodsky}.

nodes.name: Frobenius homology and Kato homology
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an abelian group. \begin{enumerate} \item We define $H_i^c(X,A(n))$ to be $H_i({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)\otimes A)$. \item We define Frobenius homology $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ to be the homology of the double complex $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A \xrightarrow{\varphi-1} {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A.$$ Here $\varphi$ acts covariantly in $\bar X$ on cycles on $\bar X\times \Delta^i$; the left and right hand complexes sit in homological degrees $1$ and $0$, respectively. \item The Kato homology $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ is defined to be the homology of the complex of coinvariants $\big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Defines cycle homology, Frobenius homology (cone of phi-1 on the cycle complex over the closure) and Kato homology (coinvariants).
nodes.label: def1

nodes.name: Frobenius homology with finite coefficients is Galois cohomology
nodes.statement: Note that $H_i^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$ is isomorphic to $H^{1-i}(Gal({{\mathbb F}}_q),{{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)(\bar X))$ because with torsion coefficients, Galois cohomology can be calculated by the complex above.

nodes.name: Vanishing and descent sequences for Frobenius homology
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i<2n$. We have $H_{2n}^c(X,A(n))\cong CH_n(X)\otimes A$ and $$H_{2n}^K(X,A(n))\cong H_{2n}^F(X,A(n)) \cong \big( CH_n(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G.$$ For all $i$, there are short exact sequences \begin{equation} 0\to H_i^c(\bar X,A(n))_G\to H_i^F(X,A(n))\to H_{i-1}^c(\bar X,A(n))^G \to 0. \end{equation}
conclusions: The groups $H_i^c(X,A(n))$, $H_i^F(X,A(n))$ and $H_i^K(X,A(n))$ vanish for $i<2n$.
We have $H_{2n}^c(X,A(n))\cong CH_n(X)\otimes A$
there are short exact sequences
nodes.statement_short: The three homologies vanish below degree 2n, are Chow groups in degree 2n, and Frobenius homology sits in Galois descent sequences.

conclusions: We have an exact sequence

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement: This comes from the short exact sequence of double complexes $$\begin{CD} \big( {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G@>>> {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A@>>> 0 \\ @VVV @V\varphi-1 VV@VVV \\ 0@>>> {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A @>>> \big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G \end{CD}$$ and ${{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(X)\otimes A\cong \big({{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)^G$. Functoriality and the localization property are well-known for cycle complexes, and this carries over to $\big( {{\mathbb Z}}^c(n)(\bar X)\otimes A\big)_G$ by an easy diagram chase. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: From a short exact sequence of double complexes; functoriality and localization by a diagram chase.

nodes.name: Frobenius cohomology of a finitely generated field
nodes.statement: For a finitely generated field $K$ of transcendence degree $d$ over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$, define $H^i_F(K,A(j))$ to be $\operatornamewithlimits{colim} H_{2d+1-i}^F(U,A(d-j))$, where $U$ runs through smooth schemes with function field $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Frobenius cohomology of a function field as colimit over smooth models.

nodes.statement: By \eqref{yyy}, the cohomology groups of $K$ lie in short exact sequences \begin{multline} 0\to H^{s-t-1}_{\mathcal M}(K\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,A(s-n))_G \to H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))\to \\ H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(K\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q,A(s-n))^G\to 0, \end{multline} where $K\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q$ is a finite product of fields.
conclusions: the cohomology groups of $K$ lie in short exact sequences

nodes.name: Niveau spectral sequences
nodes.statement: We have functorial spectral sequences \begin{align*} E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t}^c(X,A(n));\\ \bar E^1_{s,t}=\bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} H^{s-t}_F(k(x),A(s-n))&\Rightarrow H_{s+t+1}^F(X,A(n)).\\ \end{align*}
conclusions: We have functorial spectral sequences
nodes.statement_short: Niveau (coniveau) spectral sequences from motivic/Frobenius cohomology of residue fields to c- and Frobenius homology.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement: This follows with the niveau filtration, together with the fact that $$H_{s+t}^c(K,A(n)):= \operatornamewithlimits{colim}_{U} H_{s+t}^c(U,A(n)) \cong H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(K,A(s-n))$$ and $H_{s+t+1}^F(K,A(n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(K,A(s-n))$ for a field $K$ of transcendence degree $s$ over the base field. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: Niveau filtration together with the identification of homology of a field with its motivic/Frobenius cohomology.

nodes.name: Finite generation conjecture (homological)
nodes.statement: The groups $H_i^c(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, $H_{i}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and $H_{i}^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.
conclusions: The groups $H_i^c(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$, $H_{i}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and $H_{i}^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ are finitely generated for any $i, n$ and $X$.
nodes.label: mainhom

nodes.name: Reduction to smooth proper X
nodes.statement: By localization, it suffices to consider the case of smooth and proper $X$ (assuming that every finitely generated field over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ has a smooth and proper model).

nodes.name: Parshin's conjecture $P_n$
nodes.statement: Recall from \cite{ichparshin} Parshin's conjecture $P_n$, stating that $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$ and $X$ smooth and projective.
conclusions: $CH_n(X,i)$ is torsion for $i\not=0$

nodes.name: Motivic vs Frobenius cohomology of fields under Parshin
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture $P_n$. Then $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ for $t\geq n$. For $t=n-1$, the left hand side vanishes, and $H^{s-n+1}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong K_{s-n}^M(k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q)_G$. For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.
conclusions: $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ for $t\geq n$.
For $t=n-1$, the left hand side vanishes, and $H^{s-n+1}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\cong K_{s-n}^M(k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q)_G$.
For $t<n-1$, both sides vanish.
nodes.label: pupl

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.6
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the second map and the composition $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism for $t\geq n-1$ by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. By Parshin's conjecture, the groups $H^i_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n))$ are torsion for $i<s-n$, so that Galois cohomology and cohomology of the Weil-group $G$ agree for those groups. The result now follows with the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures by comparing \eqref{frobdescent} with the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence for Galois cohomology (for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$). \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Frobenius descent sequence with Hochschild-Serre using Beilinson-Lichtenbaum and Parshin's torsion statement.

nodes.name: Kato complex
nodes.statement: We define the Kato complex $KC_n(X)$ of weight $n$ to be the complex $$ \bigoplus_{X_{(n)}} {{\mathbb Z}} \gets \bigoplus_{X_{(n+1)}} (k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q)^\times_G \gets \cdots\gets \bigoplus_{X_{(s)}} K_{s-n}^M(k(x)\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q)_G \gets\cdots,$$ with the summand indexed by $X_{(s)}$ in degree $s-n$. The differentials are induced by boundary maps of higher Chow groups of discrete valuation rings.
nodes.statement_short: The Kato complex of weight n: sums over points of coinvariant Milnor K-groups of residue fields over the closure.

nodes.name: Kato homology via Kato complex
nodes.statement: Assuming conjecture $P_n$, we have $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$ In particular, $H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.
conclusions: $$H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H_{i-2n}(KC_n(X)).$$
In particular, $H_i^K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes unless $2n\leq i\leq n+d$.

nodes.statement: Compare the spectral sequences of Proposition \ref{ssprop} and use Proposition \ref{pupl}. \hfill $Q.E.D.$

nodes.name: Cap-product map to $Rf^!\mu_m^{\otimes -n}$
nodes.statement: If $p\not| m$ and $k$ contains the $m$-th roots of unity, then cap-product with ${{\mathbb Z}}/m(1)(k)\cong \mu_m(k)$, defines a map $f^*\mu_m\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)\to {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n-1)$ of complexes of sheaves on $X/k$, inducing a map $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)\to f^*\mu^{\otimes -n}_m\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(0) \cong f^* \mu^{\otimes -n}_m\otimes Rf^!Z/m \cong Rf^!\mu^{\otimes -n}_m.$$
nodes.statement_short: Cap-product with mu_m gives a map from the cycle complex Z^c/m(n) to Rf^! mu_m^{-n}.

nodes.name: The cap-product map is not an isomorphism for n>0
nodes.statement: This map is in general not an isomorphism for $n>0$; for example, the left hand side vanishes for $n>\dim X$, but the right hand side is periodic in $n$.

nodes.name: The map gamma from Frobenius to etale homology
nodes.statement: This construction induces a a map $$ {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n)(\bar X) \to R\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X, {{\mathbb Z}}^c/m(n))\to R\Gamma_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,Rf^!\mu^{\otimes -n}),$$ hence $$\gamma: H_{i+1}^F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))\to H_i^{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(n))$$ by taking the cone of $\varphi-1$.
nodes.statement_short: The cap-product map induces gamma from Frobenius homology to etale homology by taking the cone of phi-1.

nodes.name: Finiteness conjecture for n=0
nodes.statement: Let $n=0$. Then Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$ under resolution of singularities.
conclusions: Conjecture \ref{finitehom} holds for $p\not| m$, and for any $m$ under resolution of singularities.
nodes.label: KJS

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.13
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite. If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities. To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$. In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: Prime-to-p: gamma is an isomorphism (duality) and Kato homology finite by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito; p-part: devissage to smooth proper and duality.

nodes.name: Comparison of motivic, Frobenius and etale cohomology of fields mod m
nodes.statement: For $k$ a field of transcendence degree $s$ over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ and $p\not|m$, $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\cong H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n)) \cong H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,\mu_m^{\otimes s-n}) $$ for $t\geq n$. nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.15
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that the maps $$H^{s-t}_{\mathcal M}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))\to H^{s-t}_F(k,{{\mathbb Z}}(s-n)) \to H^{s-t}_{\text{\rm et}}(k,{{\mathbb Z}}/m(s-n))$$ are isomorphism for $t\geq n$. The total composition is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures. Comparing the sequences \eqref{frobdescent} and \eqref{galoismodm}, it follows that the second map is an isomorphism by the Beilinson-Lichtenbaum conjectures for the finite product of fields $k\otimes_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}\bar{{\mathbb F}}_q$. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: Beilinson-Lichtenbaum for the composite, then compare the Frobenius and Galois descent sequences.

nodes.statement: We get an exact sequence $$H^{2n-2}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to \ker f\to \ker g\to H^{2n-1}_K(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n)) \to \operatorname{coker} f\to \operatorname{coker} g \to 0.$$ By Corollary \ref{tatecor} below, $f$ has conjecturally the same kernel and cokernel as the cycle map, whereas $g$ is related to the cycle map over the algebraic closure: $$ \begin{CD} 0@>>> H^{2n-1}_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))_G @>>> H^{2n}_F(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> CH^n(\bar X)^G @>>> 0\\ @III @VVV @Vg VV @VVV \\ 0@>>> H^{2n-1}_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))_G @>>> H^{2n}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^G @>>> 0 \end{CD}$$ Thus Kato homology measures the difference of the failure of the integral Tate conjecture over ${{\mathbb F}}_q$ and over its algebraic closure.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.1
nodes.statement: $a)\Rightarrow c)$ This follows because $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\cong H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and the former vanishes for $i\not=2n$ by hypothesis. To show the equivalence of a) and b) we can assume Parshin's conjecture, and consider the exact sequence of \cite{ichweilI} $$ \cdots \to H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^i_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{i-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\to \cdots.$$ Then a) and b) imply each other for $i\leq 2n$ and $i>2n+2$, and we are left with \begin{multline*} 0\to H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))\\ \to H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to H^{2n+2}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0 . \end{multline*} By the Weil-conjectures and counting coranks one sees that the corank $C$ of $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\cong H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ and of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ agree. a) $\Rightarrow$ b): Finiteness of $H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ implies that $C$ agrees with the dimension of $H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n))$, and since $H^{2n+2}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion, $H^{2n+1}_W(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))/{\text{\rm tor}}$ must be a lattice of the same rank. nodes.name: Factorization of the l-adic cycle map
nodes.statement: Using the functorial identification ${{\mathbb Z}}/m(n)\cong \mu_m^{\otimes n}$ for $\operatorname{char} k\not| m$ of \cite{bkbl} and ${{\mathbb Z}}/p^r(n)\cong \nu_r^n[-n]$ of \cite{marcI}, the $l$-adic cycle map can be factored as follows: $$ c:H^i_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{v}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{w}{\hookrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n)).$$
nodes.statement_short: The l-adic cycle map factors as change of topology u, completion v and inclusion w.

nodes.name: l-adic completion and l-adic cohomology notation
nodes.statement: Here we write $A^{\wedge l}$ for the $l$-adic completion, and $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ for the $l$-adic cohomology $\operatornamewithlimits{lim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}/l^r(n))$ to distinguish it from the hypercohomology of ${{\mathbb Z}}(n)\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the completion map
nodes.statement: The completion map $v$ is surjective.
conclusions: The completion map $v$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: The ${{\mathbb Z}}_l$-module $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l}\subseteq H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ is finitely generated and the cokernel of $v$ is $l$-divsible by \cite[(4.2)]{jannsencont}, hence must be trivial. \hfill $Q.E.D.$

nodes.name: Kernel-cokernel sequence for the cycle map
nodes.statement: We have an exact sequence \begin{multline*} 0\to \ker u\to \ker c\to {\rm div}\; H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \\ \to \operatorname{coker} u\to \operatorname{coker} c\to T_lH^{i+1}(X_{\text{\rm et}},{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\to 0. \end{multline*} The groups $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker} u$ are torsion.
conclusions: We have an exact sequence
The groups $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker} u$ are torsion.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement: This is the kernel-cokernel sequence of the composition $c= (wv)\circ u$. The kernel of $wv$ is the kernel of $v$, which is the group of divisible elements of $H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}_l$. The cokernel of $wv$ is the Tate module $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: Kernel-cokernel sequence of the composition c = (wv) o u.

nodes.name: Kernel and cokernel of u equal those of the cycle map
nodes.statement: Under Conjecture \ref{lichtconj}, the kernel and cokernel of $u$ are equal to the kernel and cokernel of the cycle map, respectively.
conclusions: the kernel and cokernel of $u$ are equal to the kernel and cokernel of the cycle map, respectively.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.4
nodes.statement: If $i\not=2n$, then all groups in the factorization of $c$ are expected to be finite, and $v$ and $w$ are isomorphisms. The cycle map $CH^n(X)\otimes {{\mathbb Z}}_l\to H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))$ is rationally surjective if and only if $T_lH^{i+1}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ vanishes, hence Tate's conjecture is equivalent to $\operatorname{Div} H^{2n+1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ torsion free. It is rationally injective (Beilinson's conjecture) if and only if $\operatorname{div} H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))$ is torsion. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
nodes.statement_short: For i != 2n all groups finite and v, w isomorphisms; for i = 2n relate surjectivity/injectivity to Tate and Beilinson conjectures.

nodes.name: Cokernel of u via r and s
nodes.statement: Considering the diagram $$\begin{CD} H^{2n-1}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n)) @>surj>> H^{2n}_{\mathcal M}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\\ @VrVV @VuVV @| @VsVV \\ H^{2n-1}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>inj>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))@>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}(n)) @>>> H^{2n}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,{{\mathbb Q}}/{{\mathbb Z}}(n)), \end{CD}$$ we obtain a short exact sequence $0\to \operatorname{coker} r\to \operatorname{coker} u\to \ker s\to 0$, and all three groups are conjecturally finite.

nodes.name: Base-changed cycle composition
nodes.statement: Let $X_r=X\times_{{{\mathbb F}}_q}{{\mathbb F}}_{q^r}$, $G_r=Gal(\bar {{\mathbb F}}_q/{{\mathbb F}}_{q^r})$ and consider the colimit over the composition \begin{multline} H^i_{\mathcal M}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{v}{\twoheadrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{w}{\hookrightarrow}\\ H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))\stackrel{x}{\twoheadrightarrow} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))^{G_r}. \end{multline}

nodes.name: Colimit cycle map over the algebraic closure
nodes.statement: It is clear that the first two groups commute with the colimit in $r$, so if we write $\gamma_*M=\operatornamewithlimits{colim} M^{G_r}$ for the largest continuous submodule of a Galois-module, then the colimit takes the form \begin{multline} \bar c: H^i_{\mathcal M}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{\bar u}{\to} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))\otimes{{\mathbb Z}}_l \stackrel{\bar v}{\twoheadrightarrow} \operatornamewithlimits{colim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,{{\mathbb Z}}(n))^{\wedge l} \stackrel{\bar w}{\hookrightarrow}\\ \operatornamewithlimits{colim} H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(X_r,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n))\twoheadrightarrow \gamma_* H^i_{\text{\rm et}}(\bar X,\hat{{\mathbb Z}}_l(n)). \end{multline}

nodes.name: Parshin makes the groups torsion
nodes.statement: For the second map, we compare \eqref{frobdescent} to the analog short exact sequence for etale cohomology. nodes.name: Prime-to-p case via duality and Jannsen-Kerz-Saito
nodes.statement: If $n=0$, then $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by \cite{ichduality}, hence Frobenius homology is finite. But by Jannsen-Kerz-Saito \cite{kerzsaito}, Kato homology is finite.

nodes.name: p-primary case via devissage and duality
nodes.statement: If $m=p^r$, then Kato homology is finite under resolution of singularities. To show finiteness of Frobenius homology, one reduces by the usual devissage to the case that $X$ is smooth and proper of dimension $d$. In this case, $\gamma$ is an isomorphic to the finite group $H^{d-i}_{\text{\rm et}}(X,\nu^{d}_r)$ by Theorem \ref{dduuaall} and the isomorphism ${{\mathbb Z}}^c/p^r(0) \cong \nu^d_r[d]$. \hfill $Q.E.D.$
